claims.text: Below 300°C, Pt-, Ir-, or Ru-derived precursors reduce before Ni-, Co-, Cu-, and Fe-derived precursors.
The initially reduced Pt, Ir, or Ru forms a stable noble-metal lattice.
The noble-metal lattice promotes adsorption and dissociation of H2.
Reactive hydrogen generated on the noble-metal lattice reduces neighboring Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe ions.
Sequential hydrogen-assisted reduction incorporates Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe into the preformed noble-metal lattice.
Sequential reduction enables formation of a single-phase solid solution.
Initial reduction of Pt–Ru-containing material at 300°C favors a kinetically trapped Pt-based fcc phase.
The activation barrier for the proposed fcc-to-hcp transformation is approximately 0.45 eV.
Secondary heating at 400–500°C supplies sufficient energy to overcome the proposed fcc-to-hcp transformation barrier.
The hcp structure is thermodynamically favored for the Ru-rich phase.
Increasing Ru content and applying secondary heating at 400–500°C will increase the Ru-hcp phase fraction.
The phase evolution produces porous, self-supported three-dimensional nanoframeworks assembled from nanoarms.
Coexisting Pt-based fcc and Ru-based hcp domains mediate the final crystallographic structure.
The resulting porous three-dimensional nanoframework will have a larger electrochemically active surface area than the Pt-rich fcc baseline and commercial Pt black.
The resulting material will have higher methanol-oxidation activity than the Pt-rich fcc baseline and commercial Pt black.
Commercial Pt black has a methanol-oxidation mass activity of 170 mA/mgPt and an ECSA of approximately 17.59 m²/gPt.
The proposed mechanism does not apply to Pd-containing mixtures because Pd has unfavorable hydrogen desorption behavior.
Noble-metal-free NiCoCuFe formulations undergo phase separation or incomplete reduction under comparable conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis presents formation of a single-phase solid solution as the result, whereas the structural mediator and predicted outcome describe coexistence of distinct Pt-fcc and Ru-hcp domains and deliberate tuning of their proportions.

The predicted-outcome field calls the 300°C product a single-phase fcc material, while the baseline field describes it only as predominantly Pt-based fcc, leaving its single-phase status internally inconsistent.
